findings.text: The row-width repair is a write outside the node's declared write paths (reckon, tests, docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround): it is the only place the measured 12.5 px shortfall can be paid and the manifest declares it under over_fence_reason with coverage from tests/test_spa_project_visibility.py:161, but the change still lands outside the grant the node was fenced to, so the coordinator has to accept the over-fence rather than read the diff as in-scope.

The readiness deadline raised from 45000 to 120000 carries no assertion of its own: the only added guard, tests/test_spa_browser_harness.py:185, ties the process budget to the deadline by an inequality (timeout * 1000 > deadline), so reinstating `const deadline = Date.now() + 45000;` beside the 180 s budget still passes that test, and the visibility cases redden only against a cold served process, which gate-base.log shows is a 129 s run rather than a deterministic failure of the whole suite.

The fragment's 'at head' figure, `14 passed in 140.98 s`, is taken from gate-head-uncommitted-tree.log, whose own header names revision cb557f97 in a modified worktree, while the committed head run is gate-head.log at 6ce822cf with `14 passed in 136.47s` (and the -head.txt kept beside the fragment names 673960cf, 137.13 s); the quoted number therefore does not belong to the revision the fragment describes, so the citation cannot be reconciled with the run's own gate log.
